q: The waxy layer covering the epidermis, generally absent in roots, is called the:
The cuticle is the waxy covering of aerial epidermis; it is absent in roots.
A group of different tissues associated to perform a common function is called a:
A tissue system is several different tissues working together, e.g. the epidermal tissue system.
The guard cells of a stomatal apparatus are typically ___ shaped in most dicots.
Dicot guard cells are bean-shaped; dumb-bell shaped guard cells are seen in grasses.
In grasses, the guard cells of the stomatal apparatus are characteristically:
Grass guard cells are dumb-bell shaped, unlike the bean-shaped guard cells of most dicots.
Epidermal hairs found on the stem are called:
Trichomes are multicellular stem hairs that reduce water loss during transpiration.
Root hairs are unicellular outgrowths of epiblema cells, unlike the multicellular trichomes of the stem.
Which of these is NOT part of the ground (fundamental) tissue system?
The vascular bundle belongs to the vascular tissue system, not the ground tissue system.
In leaves, the ground tissue system is represented by the:
In leaves, the ground tissue system is represented by the mesophyll.
A vascular bundle is fundamentally composed of:
A vascular bundle = xylem + phloem; cambium is present only in open bundles, not always.
The meristematic cell layer between xylem and phloem in a dicot vascular bundle is the:
This cambium lying within the vascular bundle is called intrafascicular (vascular) cambium.
A vascular bundle with cambium present between the xylem and phloem is called:
Presence of cambium defines an open vascular bundle, capable of secondary growth.
Closed vascular bundles, incapable of secondary growth, are typically found in:
Closed vascular bundles (no cambium) are a hallmark of monocots.
When xylem and phloem lie on the same radius, with phloem usually outer to xylem, the arrangement is called:
This same-radius arrangement is termed conjoint, common in stems and leaves.
A radial arrangement of vascular tissue, where xylem and phloem alternate on different radii, is characteristic of:
Radial vascular bundles, with xylem and phloem on alternating radii, are found in roots.
In root anatomy, the outermost single layer bearing unicellular root hairs is specifically termed the:
The root's epidermis is specifically called the epiblema, a single layer producing root hairs.
Casparian strips, made of suberin, are found on the walls of:
Casparian strips are waxy suberin deposits on the radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells.
All tissue on the inner side of the endodermis in a root — pericycle, vascular bundle and pith — is together called the:
This composite region is called the stele.
Lateral roots and, later, vascular cambium originate from the:
The pericycle initiates both lateral roots and the vascular cambium during secondary growth.
In a dicot root, protoxylem lies towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the centre — this condition is called:
Protoxylem-outward, metaxylem-inward is termed exarch, typical of roots.
The number of xylem patches typically seen in a dicot (e.g. sunflower) root is:
Dicot roots usually show 2 to 4 xylem patches (monoarch to oligoarch).
The pith in a typical dicot root is:
The dicot root's pith region is small or inconspicuous, unlike the monocot root.
The vascular bundle in a dicot root shows which arrangement?
Root vascular bundles are radial, with xylem and phloem on alternating radii.
Secondary growth in a dicot root begins when:
A cambium ring forms between xylem and phloem
A cambium ring developing between xylem and phloem (from the pericycle) initiates secondary growth.
Which is the correct outside-to-inside order of regions in a dicot root T.S.?
From outside inward: Epiblema (epidermis), Cortex, Endodermis, Stele.
Cortex cells in a dicot root are:
The root cortex is made of thin-walled parenchyma with intercellular spaces.
Which plant's root is commonly used to study typical dicot root anatomy?
Sunflower root is the classic example used to study dicot root anatomy.
A vascular bundle with more than six xylem patches is termed:
More than six xylem patches defines the polyarch condition, typical of monocot roots.
The pith of a monocot root is:
Unlike the dicot root, the monocot root pith is large and well developed.
The endodermis in a monocot root, like in a dicot root, shows:
Both dicot and monocot root endodermis bear Casparian strips of suberin.
In a monocot root, xylem is:
Monocot root xylem, like dicot root xylem, is exarch.
Root hairs in a monocot root are outgrowths of:
Root hairs arise from epiblema (epidermal) cells.
How many main regions are visible in a T.S. of monocot root?
Four main regions: epidermis (epiblema), cortex, endodermis, stele.
The pericycle of a monocot root is made of:
The pericycle is a single layer of thin-walled parenchyma, as in the dicot root.
A T.S. showing 9 separate xylem patches around a large central pith belongs to a:
9 xylem patches (polyarch) with a large pith is characteristic of a monocot root.
Vascular bundles in a monocot root are arranged:
Root vascular bundles, in both dicots and monocots, are radial.
Which of these root features is shared by BOTH dicot and monocot roots?
Both dicot and monocot roots show exarch protoxylem; pith size, xylem number and secondary growth differ.
Which best explains why monocot roots stay thin throughout their life?
Lack of a functional vascular cambium
No vascular cambium means no secondary xylem/phloem, so the root cannot thicken.
The cortex in a monocot root is composed mainly of:
Root cortex, in both dicots and monocots, is parenchymatous with intercellular spaces.
The hypodermis of a dicot stem, giving mechanical strength to the young stem, is composed of:
The dicot stem hypodermis is made of collenchyma, allowing flexible mechanical support.
The endodermis of a dicot stem is also called the:
Being rich in starch grains, the dicot stem endodermis is called the starch sheath.
Vascular bundles in a dicot stem T.S. are arranged:
Dicot stem vascular bundles form a characteristic ring.
The vascular bundles of a dicot stem are:
Dicot stem vascular bundles are conjoint, open (cambium present), and endarch.
The pericycle of a dicot stem is made of:
Unlike the root, the dicot stem pericycle occurs as sclerenchymatous semi-lunar patches.
The pith of a dicot stem is:
The dicot stem has a large, central, parenchymatous pith.
'Endarch' xylem, as seen in the dicot stem, means:
Xylem alternating with phloem on different radii
Endarch means protoxylem lies towards the centre, metaxylem towards the periphery.
Epidermal appendages of a dicot stem may include:
Multicellular trichomes and a few stomata
The dicot stem epidermis may bear multicellular trichomes and a few stomata.
The cortex of a dicot stem consists of two sub-zones, namely:
Dicot stem cortex is divided into an outer hypodermis and an inner cortical (ground tissue) layer.
In a dicot stem, which layer lies between the cortex and the pericycle?
The endodermis (starch sheath) is the innermost cortical layer, lying just outside the pericycle.
The vascular bundles of a dicot stem, taken together in a ring, enclose a central:
The ring of vascular bundles surrounds the central pith.
Which of these tissues gives young dicot stems flexible mechanical support just below the epidermis?
Collenchyma in the hypodermis gives flexible support to the young, still-elongating stem.
The hypodermis of a monocot stem is made of:
Monocot stem hypodermis is sclerenchymatous, unlike the collenchymatous dicot stem hypodermis.
Vascular bundles in a monocot stem are:
Monocot stem vascular bundles are scattered through the ground tissue.
Each vascular bundle in a monocot stem is surrounded by a:
A sclerenchymatous bundle sheath surrounds each vascular bundle in the monocot stem.
Vascular bundles in a monocot stem are:
Monocot stem vascular bundles are conjoint and closed (no cambium).
Pith in a typical monocot stem is:
Since ground tissue is undifferentiated, monocot stems lack a distinct pith.
Phloem parenchyma in a monocot stem's vascular bundle is:
Phloem parenchyma is characteristically absent in monocot stems.
Water-containing cavities within a monocot stem's vascular bundle occur where:
These cavities form at the site of broken-down protoxylem elements.
Peripheral vascular bundles in a monocot stem, compared to central ones, are generally:
Peripheral bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.
Xylem in the vascular bundles of a monocot stem is:
Monocot stem xylem is endarch, as in all stems.
Ground tissue in a monocot stem is:
Not differentiated into cortex and pith
Ground tissue in the monocot stem is one undifferentiated mass, not split into cortex and pith.
A T.S. shows a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, numerous scattered closed vascular bundles and no distinct pith. This is a:
These are all classic monocot stem features.
Can vascular bundles in a monocot stem add new xylem/phloem with age?
No, because they are closed bundles
Yes, but only in the pith
Closed bundles lack cambium, so no secondary vascular tissue can be added.
The epidermis of a monocot stem is covered with a:
The monocot stem epidermis bears a thick protective cuticle.
Which of these is characteristic of monocot stems but NOT dicot stems?
Absence of phloem parenchyma is a monocot stem feature, not seen in dicot stems.
A dicot leaf, with distinct upper and lower surfaces, is described as:
Dicot leaves, with differentiated mesophyll on two distinct faces, are dorsiventral.
Palisade parenchyma in a dicot leaf is located:
Palisade parenchyma lies just below the adaxial (upper) epidermis.
Oval/round and loosely arranged with air spaces
Spongy parenchyma is loosely arranged with large intercellular air spaces.
In a dicot leaf, stomata are generally more numerous on the:
The abaxial (lower) epidermis usually bears more stomata than the adaxial surface.
The bundle sheath around a leaf's vascular bundle is made of:
The bundle sheath is a parenchymatous layer surrounding the vascular bundle.
The vascular bundle of a dicot leaf is:
Leaf vascular bundles, in both dicots and monocots, are conjoint and closed.
Vascular bundles in a leaf are seen in the:
Leaf vascular bundles run through the veins and the midrib.
Which mesophyll layer is chiefly responsible for maximum light capture in a dicot leaf?
Vertically packed palisade cells, closest to the light source, capture the most light.
Air cavities in a dicot leaf are mainly found:
Large air cavities occur between the loosely arranged spongy mesophyll cells.
The type of venation typically seen in dicot leaves is:
Dicot leaves typically show net-like, reticulate venation.
Which epidermis of a dicot leaf usually has fewer (or no) stomata?
The adaxial (upper) epidermis usually has fewer stomata, sometimes none.
Sub-stomatal cavities in a dicot leaf lie directly:
Below the stoma, adjoining spongy mesophyll
Sub-stomatal cavities sit just internal to the stoma, connecting to the spongy mesophyll air spaces.
Both epidermal layers of a dicot leaf are covered with a:
Both adaxial and abaxial epidermis bear a conspicuous waxy cuticle.
The green, expanded photosynthetic tissue between the two epidermal layers of a leaf is the:
The mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue sandwiched between the two epidermal layers.
A monocot leaf, similar in structure on both surfaces, is described as:
Monocot leaves, similar on both faces, are termed isobilateral.
Bulliform cells are located on the:
Bulliform cells occur on the adaxial epidermis, along the veins, in grasses.
Bulliform cells cause the leaf to curl when they become:
Water loss makes bulliform cells flaccid, and their collapse curls the leaf inward.
Mesophyll in a monocot leaf is:
Monocot leaf mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy types.
Stomata in a typical monocot (isobilateral) leaf are distributed:
Isobilateral leaves show roughly equal stomatal distribution on both surfaces.
Venation in monocot leaves is typically:
Monocot leaves characteristically show parallel venation.
The vascular bundle of a monocot leaf is:
Like the dicot leaf, the monocot leaf's vascular bundle is conjoint and closed.
The adaptive significance of leaf rolling via bulliform cells is to:
Reduce exposed surface area and conserve water
Rolling reduces the exposed transpiring surface area, conserving water.
In monocot leaves, xylem in the vascular bundle is:
Monocot leaf xylem, like dicot leaf xylem, is endarch.
The bundle sheath in a monocot leaf is composed of:
Bundle sheath cells around a monocot leaf's vascular bundle are parenchymatous.
Which feature is unique to monocot (isobilateral) leaves among the options below?
Bulliform cells are a signature feature not seen in dicot leaves.
A leaf T.S. shows uniform mesophyll, roughly equal stomata on both faces and large empty cells along veins on the upper epidermis. This is a:
These are all classic isobilateral (monocot) leaf features, including bulliform cells.
Isobilateral leaves are commonly seen in:
Grasses, being monocots, typically show isobilateral leaves.
The waxy covering present on both epidermal surfaces of a monocot leaf is the:
Both surfaces of a monocot leaf bear a conspicuous cuticle.
Which feature indicates a root rather than a stem or leaf T.S.?
A radial vascular bundle (xylem and phloem on alternating radii) is characteristic of roots.
Which feature indicates a dicot rather than a monocot vascular bundle?
An open bundle, with cambium present, indicates a dicot.
Compared to a dicot root, a monocot root has:
More xylem patches (polyarch) and larger pith
Fewer xylem patches and smaller pith
Identical xylem number and pith size
Monocot roots are polyarch with a large, well-developed pith.
A dorsiventral leaf, with differentiated mesophyll, belongs to:
Dorsiventral leaves, with palisade and spongy mesophyll, are typical of dicots.
Which of these is TRUE for monocot leaves but not dicot leaves?
Bulliform cells are unique to monocot (isobilateral) leaves.
A T.S. shows conjoint, closed, scattered vascular bundles with no obvious pith. This is most likely a:
Scattered, closed, conjoint bundles with no pith are classic monocot stem features.
Exarch protoxylem is a root feature, common to both dicot and monocot roots.
Endarch protoxylem is a stem feature, common to both dicot and monocot stems.
Dicot leaves typically show reticulate (net-like) venation.
Which vascular bundle feature is common to BOTH dicot and monocot stems?
Both dicot and monocot stem vascular bundles are conjoint; they differ in open/closed and ring/scattered.
Choose the correct match: Open + Radial vascular bundle occurs in:
Dicot root vascular bundles are radial and open (cambium develops later for secondary growth).
Choose the correct match: Closed + Conjoint vascular bundle occurs in:
Monocot stems and leaves both show closed, conjoint vascular bundles.
Which of these pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
Monocot stems actually lack a distinct pith; a large pith is a monocot ROOT feature.
Guard cells differ from the surrounding epidermal cells mainly in possessing:
Guard cells are the only epidermal cells with chloroplasts, letting them photosynthesise and regulate turgor for stomatal movement.
Trichomes, unlike root hairs, are typically:
Trichomes are multicellular, sometimes branched, stem hairs, unlike unicellular root hairs.
A vascular bundle incapable of secondary growth, due to the absence of cambium, is termed:
Absence of cambium defines a closed vascular bundle.
The layer of dividing cells lying within a dicot vascular bundle, between xylem and phloem, is called the ______ cambium.
'Intra-' means within; this cambium lies within the fascicle (bundle), between xylem and phloem.
Which layer of the dicot root gives rise to lateral roots?
The pericycle initiates lateral root formation.
Casparian strips in the root endodermis are composed mainly of:
Casparian strips are deposits of waxy, water-impermeable suberin.
The stele of a dicot root does NOT include the:
The cortex lies outside the endodermis and is not part of the stele.
In a dicot root, protoxylem elements are located:
Exarch condition: protoxylem towards the periphery in roots.
The number of xylem and phloem patches in a typical dicot root ranges from:
Dicot roots typically show 2 to 4 xylem/phloem patches.
The vascular bundle of a monocot root, with more than 6 xylem patches, is described as:
More than six xylem patches defines the polyarch condition.
Compared to the dicot root, the monocot root pith is:
Monocot root pith is large and well developed, unlike the small dicot root pith.
Which feature is shared by both dicot and monocot roots?
Both dicot and monocot roots show exarch protoxylem; other features differ.
The pericycle of a monocot root, unlike that of a dicot root, typically:
Always gives rise to a vascular cambium
Never gives rise to a vascular cambium
The monocot root pericycle never differentiates into a vascular cambium.
A root vascular bundle with more than six xylem patches is described as ______.
Polyarch xylem plus a large pith is a monocot root signature.
In the dicot stem, the layer of the cortex rich in starch grains is termed the:
The innermost cortical layer, rich in starch, is the endodermis or starch sheath.
The pericycle of the dicot stem occurs as:
Dicot stem pericycle appears as sclerenchymatous semi-lunar patches above the phloem.
The vascular bundles of a dicot stem are open, meaning they contain:
A layer of cambium between xylem and phloem
Open bundles have a cambium layer between the xylem and phloem.
Protoxylem lying towards the centre of the stem, with metaxylem towards the periphery, describes the:
This is the endarch condition, typical of stems.
The hypodermis of a young dicot stem is made of ______ tissue, which gives flexible mechanical support while allowing further elongation.
Collenchyma gives flexible support suited to a still-elongating young stem.
Which tissue forms the hypodermis, providing mechanical strength, in a monocot stem?
Vascular bundles of the monocot stem are:
Monocot stem bundles are scattered through the undifferentiated ground tissue.
The sheath surrounding each vascular bundle of a monocot stem is made of:
A sclerenchymatous bundle sheath surrounds each monocot stem vascular bundle.
Which tissue is notably absent within the vascular bundles of a monocot stem?
Phloem parenchyma is characteristically absent in monocot stem vascular bundles.
Water-containing cavities seen in monocot stem vascular bundles form due to the breakdown of:
Cavities form where protoxylem elements have broken down.
Secondary growth does not occur in a typical monocot stem because its vascular bundles are ______.
Closed vascular bundles (no cambium) mean monocot stems typically show no secondary growth.
The palisade parenchyma of a dicot leaf lies immediately below the:
Palisade cells lie just below the upper (adaxial) epidermis.
Spongy parenchyma differs from palisade parenchyma mainly in being:
Loosely arranged with large air spaces
Spongy parenchyma is loosely arranged with prominent intercellular air spaces.
In a dicot leaf, stomatal frequency is usually higher on the:
The lower (abaxial) surface usually bears more stomata.
The vascular bundle within a leaf vein is surrounded by a protective layer of parenchyma called the:
The bundle sheath surrounds and protects the leaf's vascular bundle.
Which mesophyll cell type is chiefly responsible for the bulk of photosynthesis due to maximum chloroplast packing?
Vertically packed palisade cells hold the most chloroplasts and drive most photosynthesis.
The venation pattern of a typical dicot leaf, useful in distinguishing it from a monocot leaf, is ______ venation.
Bulliform cells are best described as:
Bulliform cells are large, vacuolated, colourless epidermal cells.
The rolling up of grass leaves during water stress is caused by:
Flaccid bulliform cells lose the turgor holding the leaf flat, so it curls.
Mesophyll in an isobilateral (monocot) leaf is:
Differentiated into palisade and spongy layers
Monocot leaf mesophyll is uniform, not split into palisade and spongy types.
Stomatal distribution in a typical isobilateral leaf is:
Isobilateral leaves show stomata roughly equally on both surfaces.
The venation pattern typical of monocot leaves is:
Monocot leaves typically show parallel venation.
Bulliform cells in a monocot leaf are located specifically along the veins, on the ______ epidermis.
Bulliform cells occur along the veins on the upper (adaxial) epidermis.
The open/closed distinction of vascular bundles is based on the presence or absence of:
Open bundles have cambium; closed bundles lack it.
Monocot roots have a large, well-developed pith.
Monocot stems have a sclerenchymatous hypodermis; dicot stems have a collenchymatous one.
Which pairing is correct regarding leaf anatomy?
Dicot leaves are dorsiventral, with differentiated mesophyll; monocot leaves are isobilateral.
Endarch xylem, where protoxylem lies towards the centre, is a feature of ______ in both dicots and monocots.
Endarch protoxylem is a stem feature seen in both dicot and monocot stems.
The greater part of the plant body lying between the epidermis and the vascular tissue is called the ______ tissue system.
The ground tissue system comprises all tissue except the epidermis and the vascular bundles.
In the monocot root, the xylem is exarch and ______, having more than six xylem patches.
The monocot root xylem is polyarch — it has more than six xylem patches.
In the dicot leaf, the mesophyll is differentiated into the upper ______ parenchyma and the lower spongy parenchyma.
The mesophyll of a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf is differentiated into palisade (upper) and spongy (lower) parenchyma.
The waxy covering of the epidermis, generally absent in roots, is the:
The cuticle is the waxy layer covering aerial epidermis; roots lack it.
Guard cells in the stomatal apparatus of grasses are:
Grass guard cells are dumb-bell shaped.
A vascular bundle with cambium present, capable of secondary growth, is called:
Presence of cambium defines an open vascular bundle.
The single outer layer of the root producing root hairs is the:
The root's epidermis, called the epiblema, produces root hairs.
Casparian strips are waxy suberin deposits.
The number of xylem patches in a dicot root is typically:
Dicot roots show 2 to 4 xylem patches.
A vascular bundle with more than 6 xylem patches is:
More than 6 xylem patches defines polyarch.
Pith in a monocot root is:
Monocot root pith is large and well developed.
The hypodermis of a dicot stem is made of:
Vascular bundles in a dicot stem are arranged:
Dicot stem vascular bundles form a ring.
The endodermis of the dicot stem is also known as the:
It is rich in starch grains, hence called the starch sheath.
The hypodermis of the monocot stem is made of:
Vascular bundles in the monocot stem are:
Monocot stem vascular bundles are scattered.
Phloem parenchyma in the monocot stem's vascular bundle is:
Phloem parenchyma is absent in monocot stems.
A dicot leaf, differentiated into palisade and spongy mesophyll, is termed:
Palisade cells lie just below the:
Palisade cells lie below the adaxial (upper) epidermis.
The parenchyma layer surrounding the leaf's vascular bundle is the:
This layer is called the bundle sheath.
A monocot leaf, similar on both surfaces, is termed:
Bulliform cells are located on the:
Bulliform cells occur on the adaxial epidermis, along the veins.
Stomatal distribution in the monocot leaf is:
Isobilateral leaves show roughly equal stomata on both surfaces.
Radial vascular bundles are characteristic of:
Radial vascular bundles are found in roots.
Open vascular bundles, capable of secondary growth, occur in:
Open (cambium-containing) vascular bundles are a dicot feature.
Isobilateral leaves with undifferentiated mesophyll are typical of:
Isobilateral leaves, with undifferentiated mesophyll, are typical of monocots.
Grasses — lets them regrow after grazing.
The only dead element of phloem is:
Exarch xylem is a feature of:
Suberin bands in root endodermal cells.
Conjoint, closed vascular bundles are seen in:
Dumb-bell shaped guard cells are seen in:
Bulliform cells are found in leaves of:
Isobilateral grass leaves — they curl leaves during water stress.
Vascular bundles in a ring with cambium: the stem is a:
Scattered vascular bundles with sclerenchymatous sheath:
Xylem and phloem on different radii indicate:
Protoxylem towards the centre (stem). This is:
Bulliform cells help a grass leaf to:
Casparian strips are found in the:

Dark, hard central wood rich in tannins is:
Isobilateral leaf with same stomata both sides is a:
The meristem present between xylem and phloem is:
Name the tissue that conducts food.
Wood formed in autumn is called:
Periderm consists of phellogen, phellem and:
Name the outermost layer of the primary plant body.
